basis: Read revision 5 native SQL and lexical-barrier policy, the complete 28-proposition SQL inventory and the added cycle model. An effect marks the barrier before forwarding; an acknowledged validated cycle removes only effects at or before it, retaining newer effects. The policy conservatively closes on a rejected Q/P as required by its existing fail-closed rule.

The native SQL design remains subject to the prior revision 4 review: exact full-request admission, one top-level statement, and connection-local accepted target provenance are required. Cached classifications do not create connection-local state.
No new unresolved blocking design finding; conservative rejection can resolve protocol-name collisions described below.
implementation_acceptance_notes: PostgreSQL 16 prepared_queries uses NAMEDATALEN=64 and HASH_STRINGS; its string hash and comparison operate on at most the first 63 bytes. Distinct overlong protocol statement names can alias SQL and other protocol names despite an exact-string proxy table. Conservatively reject overlong protocol statement names for Parse, Bind and Close or model backend truncation and collisions exactly; test both cross-protocol directions and 63-byte-prefix collisions.

For native SQL classification require the first real token PREPARE or EXECUTE and exactly one ordered statement family, together with production-wide opaque/mode/function restrictions; family alone can misclassify CREATE TABLE AS EXECUTE. Extract body spans with checked UTF-8 byte offsets and preserve the exact original bytes.

Mark every forwarded Q/E before forwarding; associate ReadyForQuery with ordered Q/Sync boundaries and do not release a newer effect on an older Ready. Inspect ParameterStatus before release; test indirect pg_settings changes, multiple E, Sync ordering, failure/connection closure, and successful completion in a non-rejected session.

Run two clean proof builds bound to this exact final revision and the model hash, followed by independent real protocol, full backup/restore and runtime acceptance. Review did not run Lean builds or change runtime code.
formal_limits: Cycle proofs assume correct cycle numbering, Q/Sync to ReadyForQuery association and truthful lexical-status validation; they do not prove the actual frontend/backend implementation or PostgreSQL behavior.
Native bodyPart proves a nonempty substring, not its semantic body classification; SQL parser name and token span extraction remain trusted runtime adapter obligations.
approval_scope: Exact revision 5 bounded design only; proof build, implementation and runtime/recovery acceptance remain separate.
